A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A–E. The added appendix subsection and shifted equation/page numbers can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figure 1 report original simulations comparing one-pass and multi-pass SGD across sample sizes, model sizes, and numbers of passes.

after.justification: The original simulations remain, and Appendix A.3 adds a non-Gaussian simulation reported in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The sketched linear model, SGD updates, geometric stepsize schedule, and output rule remain unchanged. The relaxed theoretical assumptions and additional simulation do not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a synthetic non-Gaussian input scenario with independent coordinates taking values −1, 0, or 1. The original Gaussian linear-regression coverage is retained.

E2.justification: One-pass SGD remains the empirical comparator to multi-pass SGD throughout Figure 1. Figure 2 extends the same comparison pair to the new input distribution.

E3.justification: The original experimental settings and procedures are unchanged. Appendix A.3 explicitly reuses Figure 1(a)'s settings and hyperparameters; its new covariate distribution changes coverage rather than the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds a targeted robustness check of whether the favorable scaling from data reuse persists beyond Gaussian covariates. The existing sample-size, model-size, and pass-count analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report Figure 1 error bars as ±1 standard deviation over 100 independent draws of the sketch and true parameter. Figure 2 uses the same reporting practice, without a new uncertainty procedure or revised repetition count.

E6.justification: Figure 1's results are unchanged. New Figure 2 reports fitted slopes of −0.34 for multi-pass SGD and −0.26 for one-pass SGD under non-Gaussian covariates, adding results for that distinct scenario.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 introduces an approximate source condition allowing covariance comparability instead of exact eigenvector alignment, and a symmetric sub-Gaussian design condition for extending upper bounds, with supporting arguments. These substantially broaden the stated theoretical scope. Smaller edits also revise the sufficient GD stepsize bound and repair a missing matrix factor in Appendix A.2.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and main conclusion retain the same central claim: data reuse through multi-pass SGD improves sample scaling in suitable data-constrained linear-regression regimes. The headline rates and contribution remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly identifies eigenvector alignment and Gaussian requirements for lower bounds as specific limitations. Appendix A.3 discusses which assumptions can be relaxed and interprets Figure 2 as supporting the non-Gaussian extension.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 documents the added simulation's coordinate probabilities and normalization, and specifies reuse of Figure 1(a)'s settings. Existing implementation details and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hsu et al. (2012) and Zhivotovskiy (2024) to support its sub-Gaussian concentration arguments. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to earlier scaling-law research remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix A.3 and a limitations paragraph, expands the proof overview and selected proof introductions, and makes localized wording and notation edits. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the single-panel Figure 2 and updates the appendix contents. Figure 1 retains its panels, legends, axes, and caption, with limited surrounding layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The clearer proof guidance, approximate-alignment argument, and explicit limitations are useful additions. However, Figure 2's distribution contradicts its claimed compliance with Assumption 1A′: for its whitened second coordinate z, the stated probabilities imply E[exp(z)] ≈ 1.842, exceeding the required exp(1/2) ≈ 1.649. The experiment adds empirical robustness evidence but does not validate the formal extension as claimed. These benefits and the new reliability problem leave the net quality change uncertain.
